Subject: Audit log export cadence + PII redaction question

Hi Karthik / Lauren,

We're finalizing our evidence bundle for an upcoming regulatory review and need clarity on several audit/access log points before we sign the contract:

Hi Jake — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers first, then a suggested playbook. See attached "audit_export_spec.pdf" for a compact table of fields and formats.

Quick answers:
- Cadence: Redwood supports scheduled exports at hourly, daily, and weekly frequencies. Hourly exports are available for Hosted customers on a scheduled job; there is a throughput/ingress recommendation for high-volume accounts and an associated incremental cost.
- Formats: NDJSON and gzipped NDJSON are natively supported. Parquet is supported for Dedicated and Private (via export worker that writes to S3/GCS in Parquet). CSV is available but not recommended for large volumes.
- Redaction: We offer two redaction modes: 
  1) Export-time deterministic redaction (one-way hash of PII fields using customer or service key) and
  2) Redacted-view API that masks sensitive fields in the Console and UI (not irreversible).
  For compliance where irreversibility is required, we recommend export-time deterministic redaction with a customer-provided HMAC key; we record the export manifest and key-id in the audit trail.
- Retention/deletion enforcement: For Hosted, retention is enforced by the platform and deletions cascade to the internal export store. For Dedicated/Private, deletion is enforced either by the customer's object lifecycle policies (if exports land in a customer bucket) or by the on-prem agent which enforces retention windows.

Suggested playbook (short):
1) Agree on fields to redact and the redaction mode.
2) We'll provision an export job (hourly or daily) that writes to a signed S3/GCS presigned URL you control.
3) Run a 48-hour test with sample_audit_export.ndjson (attached) and validation scripts.
4) After validation, finalize the retention window in the export job and provide a deletion certificate after the first retention boundary passes.

I can jump on a 30-min call to walk through the export spec tomorrow. Which timezone works for you?

From: lauren_bennett@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: export pricing note and S3 vs console transfer

Karthik / Marissa — quick internal note to align before we confirm to Finvero:

- Pricing: Hourly NDJSON exports for Finvero's expected ingestion (est. 8GB/day) will hit our burst tier. Recommend proposing daily exports by default and offering hourly for a 30% uplift. Call this out in the SOW and include an adjustable knob for the first 30 days.
- Transfer method: Prefer pushing to customer-controlled S3 via presigned PUT to ensure Finvero owns the final artifact and lifecycle rules. For Hosted-only customers who can't accept S3, we can drop to Console-export with a 14-day signed download link—note that Console links are not suitable for automated SIEM ingestion.
- Redaction key management: If customer provides a KMS key for HMAC, we must add a line to the security appendix about key rotation policy and that rotated keys invalidate future verifiability of older exports. Recommend we advise the customer to keep a key-rotation schedule in their audit binder.

I'll add these bullets to the export_spec PDF. If you want, I can draft the SOW language for the hourly uplift.

Thanks,
Lauren

Subject: Re: Audit & Access Log export cadence, formats, and PII redaction options — next steps

Jake — thanks for the quick turn. Based on our call today, here's the plan we agreed on and acceptance criteria to close the item:

Plan:
- Exports: Daily gzipped NDJSON to your S3 bucket via presigned PUT. We'll enable an optional hourly stream for the first 14 days to validate ingestion; after that we'll revert to daily unless you request continuation.
- Redaction: We'll apply one-way HMAC redaction on email and IP fields using a customer-provided HMAC key. We logged the key-id in the export manifest; Redwood will not retain the unredacted token.
- Retention: Logs will be retained for 90 days in Redwood's export store; once exported to your S3 bucket, retention is controlled by your bucket lifecycle. For Hosted fallback copies (if any), Redwood will auto-delete copies older than 90 days and provide a deletion certificate within 72 hours of deletion.
- Evidence: We'll provide a sample_export.ndjson (attached) and a signed manifest with SHA256 checksums plus a deletion certificate after initial retention expiry.

Acceptance criteria (what Finvero should validate):
1) You can successfully download and decompress daily files and parse as NDJSON.
2) Your SIEM maps the hashed user_id and IP fields to an internal token map (if you need reversible mapping, we need a different workflow).
3) You received the export manifest and checksums and can validate file integrity.

Next steps:
- Provide the S3 presigned endpoint and the HMAC key-id you want us to use (we'll provide the HMAC key handshake instructions).
- I'll kick off the export job and schedule the 48-hour validation.

If that all looks good I'll send a short SOW addendum for the hourly uplift opt-in and include the exact export costs.

Regards,

Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
